requirement:
Authoring MUST use the `[authoring]` sections of the shared user configuration
and the selected workspace's `habeas.toml`, refining
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the authoring feature.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.user_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.structure`
Assessing a subject with `habeas author`, singly or in a batch that needs at
least one assessment, MUST require an `[authoring]` section in at least one of
these files; either section MAY be absent. No other operation requires the
section, including a batch with no assessments needed and the operations in
{cite}`requirements.authoring.deterministic_validation`.
It MUST support named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local
selection for each project. Credential-source references SHOULD be used;
explicit credentials MUST be supported under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`
rationale:
structural: No implementation roots are supplied, and `requirements.authoring.configuration` has no Implements edges. I found no structural obligation in its text that needs implementation evidence. I checked each clause for an alternative implementation that keeps the observable behavior but violates the clause.

- "Authoring MUST use the `[authoring]` sections of the shared user configuration and the selected workspace's `habeas.toml`" names the files and the section that supply settings. It does not name a library, type, signature or interface. A different loader, or a different internal representation, would read the same files and give the same results. It is observable behavior.
- "Assessing a subject with `habeas author` ... MUST require an `[authoring]` section in at least one of these files; either section MAY be absent. No other operation requires the section" states which operations fail when the section is missing. This is behavior at the command level. It does not say how the check is built.
- "MUST support named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local selection for each project" and "Credential-source references SHOULD be used; explicit credentials MUST be supported" describe what users can configure and how selection works. Any data model that supports them satisfies the text.
- The refinement of `requirements.configuration.feature_sections` is a requirement on how the authoring feature is defined and documented. Examples are its name, typed structure, keys, defaults, validation, precedence and absent-section behavior. The subject does not prescribe a type, field or interface. It leaves those details to the feature's own declarations.
- The cited requirements are context only: `requirements.configuration.user_location`, `requirements.configuration.structure`, `requirements.configuration.workspace_location`, `requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`, `requirements.authoring.deterministic_validation` and `requirements.authoring.credentials`. Citations do not create implementation obligations for this subject. Any structural obligations in them, such as `UserConfig` or `WorkspaceConfig` serialization, belong to those requirements' own assessments.

Every clause specifies observable behavior, and tests supply the evidence for it. The subject therefore needs no `{impl}` root.

behavioral: I found no test-adequacy gap for `requirements.authoring.configuration`. Each obligation maps to a marked test with assertions on the outcome. I did not request implementation source, because every obligation could be judged from the supplied tests.

**Uses the user and workspace `[authoring]` sections.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[authoring_uses_nearest_workspace_configuration_without_a_user_file]` removes the user file and puts a nearer nested `habeas.toml` under an ancestor one. It asserts that the request uses the nested file's `workspace-model` and its `api_key`, and that neither file is rewritten.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[either_existing_configuration_file_can_omit_its_authoring_section]` covers both splits. In one run only the user file carries the profile. In the other only the workspace file does, and the other file is `version = 1` only. In both runs authoring succeeds with the expected model.

**Requires an `[authoring]` section for `habeas author`, singly or in a batch that needs an assessment.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[version_only_configurations_cannot_author_needed_evidence]` makes both files `version = 1` only. It runs `author SUBJECT` and `author --all`, and for each it asserts failure, a "no authoring configuration" message, unchanged evidence, and no provider connection.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]` asserts the missing-configuration error for the single case. The error names the config file and points to the docs.

**No other operation requires the section.**
- `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[batch_fills_evidence_preserves_current_records_and_reauthors_only_changed_inputs]` covers a batch with nothing needed. It runs `author --all` once with an invalid user config file and once with no config file, and both succeed with no new requests or usage records.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[missing_or_stale_evidence_fails_validation_without_contacting_the_provider]` covers the operations in `requirements.authoring.deterministic_validation`. With both a full config and a `version = 1`-only config, it runs validation, `status --all` and the mdBook render for missing and stale evidence. Validation reports the failure, and status and render succeed without the model key. The provider is never contacted, no usage is recorded, and no evidence is authored.

**Named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local selection per project.**
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[explicit_project_and_default_selections_choose_whole_configs]` covers the default, the per-project selection, and an explicit name. It also covers an unknown name.
- `tests/configuration.rs#fn[workspace_defaults_and_configs_combine_with_existing_user_selections]` covers the combinations:
  - A workspace default is chosen over the user default.
  - A user project selection overrides the workspace default.
  - An explicit name picks a workspace config.
  - A workspace config replaces a same-named user config as a whole.
  - A workspace default naming a user config resolves to it.
  - A workspace-only setup with no user file works.
  - A missing name gives an error naming the file.
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[an_explicit_configuration_selects_the_nondefault_workspace_profile]` runs `--config alternate` through the CLI. It asserts the alternate model and key are used, not the default profile's.

**Explicit credentials supported; credential-source references preferred.** The workspace test uses a literal `api_key` and asserts it reaches the provider header. It also asserts the key is absent from the request body, the usage record, stdout and stderr. The detailed credential rules belong to the cited `requirements.authoring.credentials`, which is not reassessed here. The "SHOULD use credential-source references" clause is guidance for users, with no independent observable behavior to test here.

The cited requirements are context only and were not reassessed.

text: :::{req} configuration
Authoring MUST use the `[authoring]` sections of the shared user configuration
and the selected workspace's `habeas.toml`, refining
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections` for the authoring feature.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.user_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.structure`
Assessing a subject with `habeas author`, singly or in a batch that needs at
least one assessment, MUST require an `[authoring]` section in at least one of
these files; either section MAY be absent. No other operation requires the
section, including a batch with no assessments needed and the operations in
{cite}`requirements.authoring.deterministic_validation`.
It MUST support named configurations, workspace defaults, and a user-local
selection for each project. Credential-source references SHOULD be used;
explicit credentials MUST be supported under {cite}`requirements.authoring.credentials`.
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`
:::{req} user_location
Habeas MUST locate its per-user configuration at
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/habeas/config.toml` on Unix when XDG_CONFIG_HOME is an absolute,
nonempty path, otherwise at `$HOME/.config/habeas/config.toml`. On Windows it MUST
use `%APPDATA%/habeas/config.toml`. `HOME` and `APPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. If no usable base directory can be
determined, an operation requiring user configuration MUST fail with an
explanatory diagnostic naming the variable.
The same user configuration MUST be usable across projects. Its location MUST
NOT be selected relative to the current project or changed by project settings.
User-local preferences for a project MAY remain in the user configuration;
workspace settings MUST use `habeas.toml` under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_location`.
:::{req} structure
The user configuration file MUST be UTF-8 TOML serializing UserConfig. It MUST
contain `version = 1` and MAY contain the documented feature tables. The common
root MUST contain only the schema version and those feature tables; feature
settings MUST NOT occupy unscoped root keys. A user file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid common configuration.
Workspace configuration MUST follow {cite}`requirements.configuration.workspace_structure`.
The absence of an optional feature section MUST be distinguishable
from that feature's explicit settings and interpreted according to its own
requirements.
:::{req} deterministic_validation
Ordinary evidence validation, status inspection, and book rendering MUST continue
to check evidence using the existing rules without invoking models, contacting
providers, or requiring authoring configuration or credentials. Missing or stale
evidence MUST remain a validation failure rather than trigger authoring.
:::{req} credentials
Bedrock configurations MAY supply `credentials` containing nonempty
`access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, and optional nonempty `session_token`.
Ollama and OpenAI configurations MAY supply a nonempty `api_key`. Habeas MUST reject a
Bedrock record combining explicit credentials with `aws_profile`, and an Ollama or OpenAI
record combining `api_key` with `api_key_env`.
Explicit credentials MUST be passed directly to the selected provider without
changing process environment variables or writing credential files. Saved
explicit values MUST round-trip; credentials resolved from profiles or the
environment MUST NOT be serialized back. Debug output, configuration diagnostics,
and usage records MUST omit configured credential values. The harness MUST omit
provider credentials when constructing initial prompts. TOML
diagnostics MUST NOT echo credential-containing source lines. A configuration
file read as source, including as a prompt input, MUST follow {cite}`requirements.authoring.redaction`.
Validation MUST report a workspace `habeas.toml` present in the Git index that
contains explicit credentials, naming the file and the credential fields and
recommending credential-source references, because committed credentials leak.
Documentation MUST discourage literal credentials in workspace files and
recommend AWS profiles or environment-variable references. Examples MUST use
placeholders and explain that workspace files may be committed or read as source
when visible under the project’s `.gitignore` rules.
:::{req} workspace_location
Habeas MUST search from its invocation directory upward for the nearest enclosing
`habeas.toml`. It MUST use that file alone, without merging ancestor workspace
files. A library operation given a project root MUST search from that root unless
its current directory is inside the project, in which case it MUST start there.
The directory containing the selected file defines the base for its relative
paths; it does not replace the Cargo and mdBook project root. A missing file MUST
mean absent workspace settings. Discovery MUST report unreadable candidate files
rather than silently selecting an ancestor. Loading MUST NOT create the file.
:::{req} workspace_structure
{impl}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`
`habeas.toml` MUST serialize WorkspaceConfig as UTF-8 TOML with `version = 1`.
Its supported feature tables are `[authoring]` and
`[evidence]`; each MAY be absent. Unknown keys, unsupported versions, and invalid field types MUST produce
a diagnostic identifying the file and setting. Invalid TOML, including content
that is not UTF-8, MUST produce a diagnostic identifying the file, with the line
and column of a syntax error.
Features MUST define their own data structures and loading rules under
{cite}`requirements.configuration.feature_sections`. A file containing only
`version = 1` MUST be valid. Habeas settings MUST NOT require a `[habeas]` table
inside `book.toml`.
:::{req} feature_sections
Each configurable feature MUST define the name and typed data structure of its
user section and any supported project section, citing these common configuration
requirements. The feature MUST specify its supported keys, value types, defaults,
validation rules, and the precedence or combination rules for user settings,
project settings, and invocation options. It MUST specify the behavior of an
absent section and which operations require that section.
Feature-specific fields MUST stay within the feature's section. A feature MUST
NOT reinterpret another feature's settings or change the shared file locations
or schema version. A feature MAY define a provider-owned options map, but MUST
document that boundary and how those options are validated.
